concepts.title: Closing Stock Adjustment and Adjusted Purchases

questions.q: Calculate adjusted purchases. Use the method 'Closing Stock Adjustment and Adjusted Purchases'. Work with: closing_stock = 300, opening_stock = 24, purchases = 80000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of adjusted_purchases.

Find adjusted purchases given opening stock, purchases and closing stock. Use the method 'Closing Stock Adjustment and Adjusted Purchases'. Work with: closing_stock = 40, opening_stock = 20, purchases = 12000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of adjusted_purchases.
Explain in your own words what 'Closing Stock Adjustment and Adjusted Purchases' refers to.
questions.a: Closing stock represents the value of unsold inventory at the end of the financial period, which can either be credited to the trading account or adjusted directly through purchases.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Closing Stock Adjustment and Adjusted Purchases'.
questions.a: Closing stock is credited to trading account and shown as a current asset, or adjusted via purchases to show adjusted purchases on the debit side.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Closing Stock Adjustment and Adjusted Purchases', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate total expense to be debited to profit and loss account including outstanding amount. Use the method 'Outstanding Expenses Adjustment'. Work with: expense_paid = 20000, outstanding_expense = 50000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_expense.

Find the final expense when unpaid expense is given. Use the method 'Outstanding Expenses Adjustment'. Work with: expense_paid = 8000, outstanding_expense = 8000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_expense.
Explain in your own words what 'Outstanding Expenses Adjustment' refers to.
questions.a: Unpaid expenses incurred during the current financial period are outstanding expenses and must be added to the relevant expense head and recorded as a current liability.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Outstanding Expenses Adjustment'.
questions.a: Accrual basis mandates adding unpaid costs to current year expenses and recognizing a corresponding liability.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Outstanding Expenses Adjustment', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate net expense after deducting prepaid portion. Use the method 'Prepaid Expenses Adjustment'. Work with: expense_paid = 80000, prepaid_expense = 12000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of effective_expense.

Find insurance premium to be charged to profit and loss account. Use the method 'Prepaid Expenses Adjustment'. Work with: expense_paid = 5000, prepaid_expense = 500. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of effective_expense.
Explain in your own words what 'Prepaid Expenses Adjustment' refers to.
questions.a: Expenses paid in advance whose benefits extend into the subsequent accounting period are deducted from total expenses and presented as current assets.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Prepaid Expenses Adjustment'.
questions.a: Advance payments for future periods are excluded from current P&L expense and carried forward as assets.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Prepaid Expenses Adjustment', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate total income earned including accrued revenue. Use the method 'Accrued Income Adjustment'. Work with: accrued_income = 500, income_received = 50000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_income.

Find total commission credited to profit and loss account. Use the method 'Accrued Income Adjustment'. Work with: accrued_income = 500, income_received = 2500. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_income.
Explain in your own words what 'Accrued Income Adjustment' refers to.
questions.a: Income earned during the current period but not yet received in cash by the end of the year is added to total revenue and listed as a current asset.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Accrued Income Adjustment'.
questions.a: Revenues earned but uncollected are recognized in the profit and loss account and shown under current assets.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Accrued Income Adjustment', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate net earned income when advance receipt is included. Use the method 'Income Received in Advance Adjustment'. Work with: advance_income = 2500, income_received = 20000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of earned_income.

Find actual rent income for the current financial year. Use the method 'Income Received in Advance Adjustment'. Work with: advance_income = 500, income_received = 500. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of earned_income.
Explain in your own words what 'Income Received in Advance Adjustment' refers to.
questions.a: Revenue received during the current period that relates to future accounting periods must be deducted from current income and reported as a current liability.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Income Received in Advance Adjustment'.
questions.a: Unearned revenue collected in advance is excluded from current income and treated as a liability.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Income Received in Advance Adjustment', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate depreciation charge on fixed asset. Use the method 'Depreciation Adjustment'. Work with: asset_cost = 2500, rate = 18. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_book_value.

Find net book value of asset after depreciation. Use the method 'Depreciation Adjustment'. Work with: asset_cost = 1200, rate = 20. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_book_value.
Explain in your own words what 'Depreciation Adjustment' refers to.
questions.a: Depreciation is the reduction in book value of fixed assets due to wear, tear, and usage over time, charged as a expense in P&L and deducted from asset cost in Balance Sheet.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Depreciation Adjustment'.
questions.a: Depreciation allocates fixed asset cost as an expense, reducing net profit and asset book value.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Depreciation Adjustment', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Bad Debts and Further Bad Debts Adjustment

questions.q: Calculate total bad debts expense for profit and loss account. Use the method 'Bad Debts and Further Bad Debts Adjustment'. Work with: existing_bad_debts = 24, further_bad_debts = 20, total_debtors = 60. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_debtors.

Find remaining debtors after writing off further bad debts. Use the method 'Bad Debts and Further Bad Debts Adjustment'. Work with: existing_bad_debts = 15, further_bad_debts = 15, total_debtors = 50. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_debtors.
Explain in your own words what 'Bad Debts and Further Bad Debts Adjustment' refers to.
questions.a: Irrecoverable debts written off during the period are recorded as bad debts; additional irrecoverable amounts identified at year-end are further bad debts that reduce debtors balance.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Bad Debts and Further Bad Debts Adjustment'.
questions.a: Further bad debts increase total bad debt expense in P&L and directly reduce sundry debtors in the balance sheet.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Bad Debts and Further Bad Debts Adjustment', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Provision for Bad and Doubtful Debts Adjustment

questions.q: Calculate new provision for doubtful debts. Use the method 'Provision for Bad and Doubtful Debts Adjustment'. Work with: debtors = 3, existing_bad_debts = 20, further_bad_debts = 120, old_provision = 18, rate = 15. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of pnl_charge.

Find net debit or credit to profit and loss account for bad debts provision. Use the method 'Provision for Bad and Doubtful Debts Adjustment'. Work with: debtors = 15, existing_bad_debts = 18, further_bad_debts = 400, old_provision = 45, rate = 8. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of pnl_charge.
Explain in your own words what 'Provision for Bad and Doubtful Debts Adjustment' refers to.
questions.a: An estimated provision set aside from profits to cover potential future losses from doubtful debts, calculated as a percentage of good debtors after deducting further bad debts.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Provision for Bad and Doubtful Debts Adjustment'.
questions.a: New provision is computed on debtors after deducting further bad debts, and the net charge to P&L accounts for old provision balances.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Provision for Bad and Doubtful Debts Adjustment', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Provision for Discount on Debtors Adjustment

questions.q: Calculate provision for discount on debtors. Use the method 'Provision for Discount on Debtors Adjustment'. Work with: debtors = 6, further_bad_debts = 40, provision_doubtful = 40, rate = 20. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_realisable_debtors.

Find good debtors balance available for discount provision. Use the method 'Provision for Discount on Debtors Adjustment'. Work with: debtors = 150, further_bad_debts = 10, provision_doubtful = 20, rate = 18. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_realisable_debtors.
Explain in your own words what 'Provision for Discount on Debtors Adjustment' refers to.
questions.a: A provision created on good debtors (after deducting bad debts and provision for doubtful debts) to estimate discounts to be allowed for prompt payment in the next period.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Provision for Discount on Debtors Adjustment'.
questions.a: Discount provision is estimated only on good debtors remaining after all bad debt adjustments.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Provision for Discount on Debtors Adjustment', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate manager commission before charging such commission. Use the method 'Manager's Commission Adjustment'. Work with: profit = 8000, rate = 8. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of commission_after.

Calculate manager commission after charging such commission. Use the method 'Manager's Commission Adjustment'. Work with: profit = 500, rate = 20. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of commission_after.
Explain in your own words what 'Manager's Commission Adjustment' refers to.
questions.a: Remuneration allowed to a manager calculated as a percentage of net profits, either before or after charging such commission.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Manager's Commission Adjustment'.
questions.a: Commission before charging uses rate/100; commission after charging uses rate/(100 + rate).

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Manager's Commission Adjustment', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: commission = profit * rate / 100 OR commission = profit * rate / (100 + rate)

questions.q: Calculate interest on capital for the year. Use the method 'Interest on Capital Adjustment'. Work with: capital = 12000, rate = 25. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of interest_on_capital.

Find amount of interest on opening capital. Use the method 'Interest on Capital Adjustment'. Work with: capital = 1200, rate = 20. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of interest_on_capital.
Explain in your own words what 'Interest on Capital Adjustment' refers to.
questions.a: Interest allowed to the proprietor on capital invested in business, treated as a business expense in P&L and credited to capital account in Balance Sheet.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Interest on Capital Adjustment'.
questions.a: Interest on capital is charged to profit and loss account as an expense and added to capital in the balance sheet.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Interest on Capital Adjustment', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate interest on capital at 4% on capital of 210000. Use the method 'Interest on Capital Adjustment'. Work with: capital = 1200, rate = 12. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of interest_on_capital.

Find the interest on capital. Use the method 'Interest on Capital Adjustment'. Work with: capital = 5000, rate = 20. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of interest_on_capital.
Explain in your own words what 'Interest on Capital Adjustment' refers to.
questions.a: An adjustment made to record interest allowed on the owner's capital investment, which is treated as an expense for the business and an addition to capital.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Interest on Capital Adjustment'.
questions.a: Increases business expenses (debit P&L) and increases owner's capital in the balance sheet.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Interest on Capital Adjustment', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate depreciation on machinery at 10%. Use the method 'Depreciation on Fixed Assets'. Work with: asset_value = 8000, depreciation_rate = 12. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of depreciation_amount.

Find the depreciation on scooter. Use the method 'Depreciation on Fixed Assets'. Work with: asset_value = 5000, depreciation_rate = 10. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of depreciation_amount.
Explain in your own words what 'Depreciation on Fixed Assets' refers to.
questions.a: The systematic allocation of the cost of a tangible asset over its useful life, recorded as an expense in the Profit and Loss account and deducted from the asset value in the Balance Sheet.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Depreciation on Fixed Assets'.
questions.a: Reduces the book value of fixed assets and charges the reduction as an operating expense.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Depreciation on Fixed Assets', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate the provision for doubtful debts at 5% on debtors. Use the method 'Provision for Doubtful Debts Adjustment'. Work with: debtors = 75, further_bad_debts = 120, provision_rate = 18. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of provision_amount.

Find the provision on debtors. Use the method 'Provision for Doubtful Debts Adjustment'. Work with: debtors = 60, further_bad_debts = 24, provision_rate = 12. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of provision_amount.
Explain in your own words what 'Provision for Doubtful Debts Adjustment' refers to.
questions.a: An estimate of potential losses from credit sales that may become uncollectible, calculated as a percentage of outstanding debtors after deducting further bad debts.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Provision for Doubtful Debts Adjustment'.
questions.a: Created to adhere to the conservatism principle, reducing debtors in the balance sheet and charging P&L.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Provision for Doubtful Debts Adjustment', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Net Bad Debts Expense in Profit and Loss

questions.q: Calculate the net bad debts to be debited to profit and loss account. Use the method 'Net Bad Debts Expense in Profit and Loss'. Work with: bad_debts = 8, further_bad_debts = 5, new_provision = 15, old_provision = 100. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_bad_debts_expense.

Find the debit to Profit and Loss account for bad debts. Use the method 'Net Bad Debts Expense in Profit and Loss'. Work with: bad_debts = 3, further_bad_debts = 45, new_provision = 100, old_provision = 120. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_bad_debts_expense.
Explain in your own words what 'Net Bad Debts Expense in Profit and Loss' refers to.
questions.a: The total bad debts expense transferred to the Profit and Loss account, combining existing bad debts, further bad debts, and the new provision, while deducting the old provision.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Net Bad Debts Expense in Profit and Loss'.
questions.a: Combines all bad debt adjustments to find the net impact on the Profit and Loss account.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Net Bad Debts Expense in Profit and Loss', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate interest on drawings at 7%. Use the method 'Interest on Drawings'. Work with: drawings = 360, rate = 12. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of interest_on_drawings.
Find the interest on drawings. Use the method 'Interest on Drawings'. Work with: drawings = 8, rate = 20. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of interest_on_drawings.
Explain in your own words what 'Interest on Drawings' refers to.
questions.a: Interest charged by the business on withdrawals made by the owner for personal use, which is an income for the business and a deduction from capital.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Interest on Drawings'.
questions.a: Credited to P&L account and deducted from drawings/capital in the balance sheet.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Interest on Drawings', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate the net insurance expense after deducting unexpired insurance. Use the method 'Prepaid Expenses Adjustment'. Work with: prepaid_amount = 120000, total_paid = 500. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_expense.

Find the net expense after prepaid adjustment. Use the method 'Prepaid Expenses Adjustment'. Work with: prepaid_amount = 20000, total_paid = 50. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_expense.
Explain in your own words what 'Prepaid Expenses Adjustment' refers to.
questions.a: Expenses paid in advance during the current accounting period that relate to a future period, which are deducted from the respective expense and shown as a current asset.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Prepaid Expenses Adjustment'.
questions.a: Adjusts the expense to reflect only the current period's share.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Prepaid Expenses Adjustment', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate the total wages including outstanding wages. Use the method 'Outstanding Expenses Adjustment'. Work with: outstanding_amount = 1200, paid_expense = 80000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_expense.

Find the total expense with outstanding adjustment. Use the method 'Outstanding Expenses Adjustment'. Work with: outstanding_amount = 1200, paid_expense = 5000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_expense.
Explain in your own words what 'Outstanding Expenses Adjustment' refers to.
questions.a: Expenses incurred during the current accounting period but not yet paid, which are added to the respective expense in P&L and shown as a current liability.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Outstanding Expenses Adjustment'.
questions.a: Ensures complete matching of expenses incurred with revenues earned.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Outstanding Expenses Adjustment', in plain ASCII form.
Explain in your own words what 'Access DLookup Function' refers to.
questions.a: An Access database function used to search and retrieve a specific value from a field in a table or query based on a given search condition.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Access DLookup Function'.
questions.a: Retrieves non-local data for display in forms or reports.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Access DLookup Function', in plain ASCII form.
Explain in your own words what 'Access DSum Function' refers to.
questions.a: A domain aggregate function in Access that calculates and returns the sum of values in a specified field or expression within a table or query, optionally filtered by a criteria.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Access DSum Function'.
questions.a: Computes totals for a subset of records matching a condition.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Access DSum Function', in plain ASCII form.
Explain in your own words what 'Access IIF Function' refers to.
questions.a: A conditional function in Access that evaluates a logical expression and returns one value if the expression is true, and another value if it is false.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Access IIF Function'.
questions.a: Implements binary decision logic in queries, forms, or reports.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Access IIF Function', in plain ASCII form.
Find the absolute value of a number. Use the method 'Access Abs Function'. Work with: number = 4096. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of absolute_value.
Calculate the absolute value using Abs. Use the method 'Access Abs Function'. Work with: number = 2048. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of absolute_value.
Explain in your own words what 'Access Abs Function' refers to.
questions.a: A mathematical function that returns the absolute (positive) value of a given numeric expression, ignoring its sign.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Access Abs Function'.
questions.a: Converts negative numbers to positive while keeping positive numbers unchanged.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Access Abs Function', in plain ASCII form.
Explain in your own words what 'Access Val Function' refers to.
questions.a: A function that extracts and returns the numeric characters from a string as a numeric value, stopping at the first non-numeric character.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Access Val Function'.
questions.a: Converts string representations of numbers into actual numeric types.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Access Val Function', in plain ASCII form.
